subject: Integration prep: credentialing, routing plan, and SDK setup
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Eva Torres <eva.torres@ledgergen.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Integration prep: credentialing, routing plan, and SDK setup

Hi Eva — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can unblock the PoC and scope the Dedicated footprint if needed. Notes below focus on auth, routing, and the SDK integration you asked about.

TL;DR ask: Please confirm whether LedgerGen will use a service account approach (short-lived JWT) or long-lived API keys for the initial PoC. We recommend service accounts + short-lived tokens for production.

Summary of items discussed:
- Auth patterns: Redwood supports API keys, OAuth2/JWT service accounts, and token exchange for short-lived credentials. For regulated data we recommend customer-managed KMS + HSM-backed keys (optional with Private).
- SDK setup: We have an SDK quickstart (node/python) that supports automatic credential refresh; can instrument in ~45min for basic generation + structured output.
- Routing/cost: We can configure routing rules so lower-cost models handle non-sensitive batch workloads and higher-tier models handle low-latency chat.
- Embeddings/rerankers: We recommend a two-tier embedding index (dense + sparse) for retrieval-augmented generation; reranker only on top-K to save tokens.

Proposed next steps (action items):
1) LedgerGen to confirm credentialing approach (service account w/ JWT rotation OR API keys) — Eva
2) Redwood to share credentialing checklist + SDK snippets for token refresh — Marissa (attached)
3) Schedule a 30-min handoff with SRE to map network egress/VPC endpoints — Rishi/Ben to coordinate
4) If service accounts chosen: identify PKI/KMS owner and whether LedgerGen will provide a public key endpoint for token verification.

Attachments: redwood-api-credentialing-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-auth-patterns-diagram.png (PNG)

Thanks — I can be available tomorrow morning for a short SRE sync if that helps.

Best,
Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — super helpful recap. Quick answers from our side:

- For the PoC we'll start with API keys to move faster; production will need service accounts + rotation.
- Our security team prefers short-lived tokens for any production traffic; they asked for a sample rotation cadence and recommended TTLs.
- SRE availability: can do a 30-min window on Wed 06/23 at 08:00 PT.

Could you attach the SDK snippets inline (node/python) showing token refresh flow? Also our SRE wants a diagram of the token exchange flow so they can map to our KMS.

Eva

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Eva Torres <eva.torres@ledgergen.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-22T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration prep: credentialing, routing plan, and SDK setup

Eva — thanks. Attached two quick items: 1) SDK snippets (node/python) showing the refresh JWT flow and client-side rotation, and 2) a simple token-exchange diagram for your SRE. Key notes:

- PoC with API keys: we'll accept API keys scoped to dataset and model routes; keys can be rotated manually from the Console or via our API.
- Production path (recommended): service account -> signed JWT -> Redwood token endpoint (short-lived access token, default TTL 15m). TTL is configurable; many customers run 5-20m.
- We also support OIDC federation for enterprise IdP if you want SSO + automated provisioning.

SDK snippet (Node) — token refresh pattern (inline):
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ authEndpoint: 'https://auth.redwood.com/token', serviceAccountKey: process.env.SA_KEY });
async function getClientToken() {
  // exchange signed JWT for short-lived token
  const token = await client.exchangeServiceJWT();
  return token;
}

Python snippet (refresh):
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(auth_endpoint='https://auth.redwood.com/token', sa_key=os.environ['SA_KEY'])
# call client.exchange_service_jwt() to get short-lived token and auto-refresh

Network notes for the SRE call:
- IPs to allow: 34.198.12.0/24 (redwood egress for hosted), plus regional prefixes if using Dedicated/Private (we'll share finer CIDR on the call)
- Ports: 443 outbound for API + 5222 for optional agent heartbeat if running Dedicated host agent

I've uploaded the checklist and diagram to the Drive link in the meta. Let me know if you'd like us to pre-create a scoped API key for the PoC (we can create one that auto-expires after 30 days).

See you all Wed.
Marissa
